title: Planning-run expansion submission
description: Objective: enable the existing authoritative PlanningRun reducer to process exactly bound EXPANSION drafts and compound plan.propose submissions without weakening INITIAL behavior. Depends on task-fcad40b6d26243439cd19fd3e49c924d. Deliverable: PlanningRun validates the active hold-bound EXPANSION schema, seals one immutable multi-node proposal/refusal, and remains zero-authority until later approval. NOT in scope: REVISION support, scheduler admission, automatic approval, resource/budget preparation, graph activation, or persistence. Owned paths: packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-reducer.ts, planning-run-submission.ts, planning-run-reducer.test.ts. Production consumers: scheduler/core expansion children and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: PlanningRun accepts EXPANSION creation/proposal only when the exact active hold, parent/handoff, proposal-base hash, goal version, graph epoch, planning authority, and finalized runner boundary match; REVISION remains explicitly unsupported.

The compound submission seals the complete child/integrator proposal identity or one stable expansion refusal; malformed, stale, wrong-kind, mismatched-hold, incomplete, or changed multi-node inputs refuse with exact code and layer and leave state unchanged.

INITIAL behavior and its single-node fence remain unchanged, and no EXPANSION accepted/refused result contains child run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget allocation, graph activation, dispatch, or partial proposal authority.

Focused tests cover INITIAL compatibility, EXPANSION success, duplicate replay, refusal precedence, changed base/epoch/hold, competing finalize/cancel schedules, nonzero generated permutations, and production guard mutations with exact code plus layer.
The exact verification command exits 0, production files remain below 400 lines, and the named downstream consumers are recorded.
taskRails: Extend the existing PlanningRun authority; do not implement a parallel expansion submission reducer.
One sealed proposal is all-or-none and immutable.
Manual review remains required after submission.

comments.content:
QA evidence — task-93b0314e09f248118e21f92699989468 (qa-5be1a8d6)

- `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` — exit 0 (`tsc --project tsconfig.json`, no output).

## Mutation drill matrix — 9 drills, I ran all of them myself
Each drill: single-anchor textual mutation (abort on anchor count != 1), full suite, restore by `cmp` against a pre-drill byte copy (never by empty `git diff` — it is blind to the new file).

| drill | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `HOLD_IDENTITY_KEYS` 10 keys → `["holdId"]` | **359/359 GREEN — SURVIVES** |
| D2 | delete both `workerHandoff.digest`/`.ref` comparisons in `sameHold` | **359/359 GREEN — SURVIVES** |
| D3 | revert to `snapshotPlanningRunState` | 11 failed ✅ |
| D4 | disable `validExpansionCreateCommand` | 2 failed ✅ |
| D5 | drop `validExpansionProposeCommand` | 2 failed ✅ |
| D6 | fence unconditional `bearing.length > 1` | 1 failed ✅ |
| D7 | fence never fires | 3 failed ✅ |
| D8 | `successorData` drops `expansion` | 2 failed ✅ |
| D9 | remove INITIAL-propose-on-EXPANSION cross-kind guard | 1 failed ✅ |

Your six step-9 drills all reproduce. The two that survive are both in `sameHold` — the guard you wrote, and the only production code implementing DoD 1's central clause.

## Why D1/D2 survive — second refusal layer answers first
`proposeExpansion` (planning-run-submission.ts:97) refuses on
`!validExpansionProposeCommand(command) || !validExpansionHoldBinding(bound) || !sameHold(bound, command.expansion)`.

All three `MALFORMED_HOLDS` variants are **schema**-invalid, so `validExpansionProposeCommand` refuses before `sameHold` is ever reached:
- `NON_ACTIVE_HOLD: lifecycle "RELEASED"` — pinned constant, schema layer
- `STALE_PROPOSAL_BASE: "not-a-proposal-base-hash"` — malformed hash, not a *stale* one
- `WRONG_GRAPH_EPOCH: graphEpoch -1` — out of range, not a *different* epoch

And the one test that does reach `sameHold` — planning-run-expansion.test.ts:128 "refuses an EXPANSION proposal that swaps the run's bound hold" — varies **only `holdId`**.

Net: of the 10 compared keys, `holdId` is proven; `lifecycle` and `truthClass` are covered by the schema layer; **`generation`, `goalVersion`, `graphEpoch`, `parentNodeRef`, `parentRunRef`, `proposalBaseHash`, `sourceFingerprint`, plus both `workerHandoff` fields are asserted by nothing.** A well-formed proposal re-presenting `graphEpoch: 5` against a run held at epoch 4 is the exact input DoD 1 says must refuse, and no test would notice if it stopped refusing.

This is the project custom rail verbatim: *"a second refusal layer can start answering first and the test stays green while no longer testing its subject."*

## What makes it pass
1. Add a named `CHANGED_HOLDS` set of **well-formed** single-key deviations — one per uncovered identity field, including `workerHandoff.digest` and `workerHandoff.ref` — built off `HOLD` with values that satisfy `validExpansionHoldBinding` (use `hash(...)` for the hex fields, positive ints for the counters, real refs for the ref fields).
2. Assert each refuses with the exact code **and** layer via `expectIllegal(result, "plan.propose", "PLANNING")` — that already pins `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION` + `{aggregateKind:"PLANNING_RUN", commandKind, sourceState}`, so no new vocabulary is needed.
3. Assert the generated count is nonzero and equals the key set size, same shape as your existing `expect(keys.length).toBe(3)` — a sweep that produces zero cases passes.
4. Re-drill D1 and D2. `HOLD_IDENTITY_KEYS = ["holdId"]` must go red, and deleting the `workerHandoff` comparisons must go red. Do not ship until both do.
5. DoD 4 also names *competing finalize/cancel schedules* and no test drives `goal.cancel` or `planning.cancel` against an EXPANSION run. Note `planning-run-authority.test.ts:126` is literally named "refuses expansion-only planning.cancel from every lifecycle" yet builds only INITIAL states via `state(lifecycle)` — its named subject is now constructible and still unexercised. Add EXPANSION cases: `goal.cancel` across the permitted lifecycles, `planning.cancel` refused from every lifecycle, and cancel arriving against a sealed EXPANSION run mid-finalize.

## Verified good — do not churn these
- DoD 3 holds. The accepted EXPANSION state is exactly 14 keys (`Object.keys().sort()` pinned in both the new file and the contract test) — no lease, effect, slot, resource, budget, activation, dispatch, or partial-proposal authority anywhere in the diff.
- INITIAL compatibility holds. The `sealPlan` extraction keeps the INITIAL result byte-identical; `planning-run-authority.test.ts` untouched; the MULTI_NODE assertion at reducer.test.ts:180 green and unedited; D6/D7 prove the fence fires in exactly one direction.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE TASK'S OWN DoD 5 IS WRONG. It says 'production files remain below 400 lines'. Both owned production files live in packages/core/src/planning, which planning-source-size.test.ts hard-caps at 250 physical lines — no allowlist, no basename exception, tests and fixtures swept equally. Building to 400 there fails the suite. 250 is the bar; the DoD text is the defect.

2. THE SILENT-DEGRADE FAILURE MODE. If the snapshot swap at reducer.ts:178 is missed, EXPANSION states fail the 12-key `exact()` guard and every command returns unknownFailure() — no exception, no obviously wrong code, just UNKNOWN_ERROR. A test asserting only ok===false would pass while nothing works. Assert the full discriminated shape on every refusal, and run drill (a).

3. SUCCESSOR DEFECT, easy to ship unnoticed. successorData() builds a 12-key literal with `runKind: state.runKind`. Rejecting an EXPANSION run yields a state claiming EXPANSION with no hold binding — invalid, and only observable on the NEXT command. Step 7 closes it; without that step the task is completable and wrong.

4. NARROWING A LOOP IS NOT UPDATING A TEST. Both invalidated assertions are loops over run kinds. Deleting the EXPANSION member is correct; deleting the whole case is not, because REVISION must stay provably unsupported on both the create and propose paths. A REVISION path that quietly becomes reachable is exactly the regression DoD 1 forbids.

5. THE FENCE HAS TWO FAILURE DIRECTIONS. A fence that never fires breaks INITIAL's single-node guarantee (DoD 3); a fence that always fires blocks EXPANSION's whole purpose (DoD 2). Drills (d) and (e) test both directions deliberately.

6. AUTHORITY LEAKAGE. DoD 3 forbids any EXPANSION result carrying child run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget allocation, graph activation, dispatch or partial proposal authority. The accepted EXPANSION state adds exactly two fields — `expansion` and `sealedProposal` — and nothing else. Re-read the diff for this specifically in step 10; it is the one DoD item no test naturally catches.

7. SHARED WORKTREE. All agents work in one directory. `git diff` cannot see the new untracked test file, so never verify a mutation restore by an empty diff. A foreign whole-tree completion hook may commit your in-progress bytes; do not amend, reset or stash (epic rail 3) — report the base-ref diff over owned paths instead. Add EXPANSION cases: goal.cancel across permitted lifecycles, planning.cancel refused everywhere, cancel against a sealed EXPANSION run mid-finalize.
